turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me?
I decided, on November 3, and I should have phoned you first. That was my failure. I want to go through what I have in the order I looked at it, and I'll hand you each piece. Is that fair?
Fair enough. Go on. Hand me the first one, and tell me what it shows, the time on it included.

First, the version history. Created Wednesday October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words at 11:52 in one edit. 794 more at 11:58 in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small formatting edits. No earlier drafts. The assignment was due 8:30 Thursday.

"Wednesday the 28th, 11:31 at night. Eleven minutes after the file exists, 612 words land in one paste. Then 794 more at 11:58. Okay." I'm writing down those times. I'm not reading anything into them yet, and I'll decide what they mean when I've seen the rest. Is there anything in that history from before 11:31, or is that the start of the file?
If Owen wrote it earlier, say on paper or in another document, how would you expect him to show that? What would count for you?

"Show me the paper, the other file, or the earlier draft with its own date on it, and I'll read it myself. A handwritten page is worth more to me than a claim, if it's dated and it's his. Don't ask me to take his word for it, and don't ask me to say what the software would have to show. I'm asking you what you have."
Does Owen have a Google Drive or any other document where this was written before Wednesday night? Did he mention one at home?

"You're asking me what my son told me at home, and that's not evidence, Hale. Owen's habits aren't your case. Your case is the file. You've shown me one document, and it starts at 11:31 on a Wednesday night. Is there anything earlier, or not?"
Can you ask him tonight, and send me whatever there is, with its own date on it?

"You can ask him. I'm not going to be the one who says whether he wrote it, and I'm not going to stand here while you try to get me to. If there's a dated earlier draft, you'll have it from me in writing, and you'll also have my position in writing: the zero comes off, nothing goes on his record, and he doesn't get humiliated in front of his class again. Put in an email what you're proposing, with a deadline. Ten minutes, Hale."
How many minutes was it between the file being created and the first 612 words appearing?

"Eleven minutes. 11:31 to 11:52, by the times you read me. Eleven minutes is short for six hundred and twelve words typed by hand, and you can check that yourself. But it's a question about the times, not a finding, and I'll let you put the next document in front of me."
Second. The outline of October 15 argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and the word cowardice does not appear in it.
"Show me the outline. The date and the word are yours to prove, Hale, not mine to take. Turn the screen."

Third, the in-class piece of September 24. Forty minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

"Forty minutes, 380 words, comma splices. Nine quotations in the essay with act, scene and line. I'm writing those down. That's a difference you can see on the page, and I want to see it myself. Show me the September 24 piece, the one with his name on it."
Fourth. The essay quotes Hamlet Act 3 Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in the play.

"Then say so in writing and show me the text you checked it against. I'm not taking a quotation as fact because you've called it fake. Bring me the edition and the page, and I'll read it. If the line isn't there, that's a problem for the essay, and it's still a question of what Owen wrote and when. Fourteen minutes, Hale."
Fifth. On November 2 I asked him what epistemological paralysis means and he said 'like, being stuck'. He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph covered.
"'Like, being stuck.' Okay. I'm writing that down. Is that from a conversation you can date, with someone else in the room, or is it your memory of it?"
11:31 to 11:52 is twenty-one minutes, not eleven. Do you agree?

"You're right. Twenty-one minutes. I got that wrong, and I'll take it. Twenty-one minutes for six hundred and twelve words is still something you can check, and it's a question about the times, not a finding. What's the date and time of that meeting where he said 'like, being stuck', and who else heard it?"
The November 2 notes were written that day, in my planner, signed and dated. I can show you the page. Nobody else was in the room.

"A planner page written that day is something I can read. Show it to me, and tell me where you were when he said it. Nobody else in the room means I'm hearing one person's account, so I'll weigh it that way. Owen's answer to 'what does that mean' is a fair question for the essay, not proof of anything. What I need from you now is the in-class piece of September 24, with his name on it, and the edition with the Act 3 Scene 2 page. Ten minutes, Hale."
Sixth: the school's AI checker says 94 percent. I know your procedure says that alone is not enough, and I am not resting on it.

"Good. Then we agree the number alone isn't enough. A machine's guess is not a finding, and the company that sells that tool says the same thing. You're not resting on it, so what else is on the table, and what's your ten-minute plan for Owen's zero?"
What time is it now by your watch?
"It's still today, Hale. I'm not checking a watch for you. Owen, the essay, the zero. You've got about eight minutes before I'm standing up, so put the plan on the table."
That's the six things. What's your honest read? Where do you think the strongest point is and where the weakest?

"You're asking me where your case is weak. I'm on the other side of this table, Hale, and I'm not coaching you. Put the plan on the table: the zero comes off, nothing goes on his record, and Owen doesn't get shamed in front of his class again. Anything short of that, and I'm walking to the principal's office with the times I've written down."
I'm putting the outline, the September 24 piece and the Folger page in front of you, with his name and dates on the first two. Read them.

"I can't read anything you haven't turned toward me yet, Hale. Put them on the table and turn the first one so I can see the name and the date. And the Folger page: show me the line and the page number. Then tell me what the plan is for Owen's zero."
Do you see the difference between the outline's argument and the essay's?

"I see what you've told me about it, and that's not the same thing as seeing the pages. Turn the outline toward me, with his name and October 15 showing, and I'll tell you what I see. Then tell me what you're offering for the zero. Two minutes."

Here is my proposal. The zero comes off the gradebook now. Owen does a supervised rewrite, in my room, one period, no devices. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. If he wants to bring a parent or the counsellor, fine.

"Okay. Some of that is what I asked for, and some of it isn't yet. The zero comes off today, in the gradebook, before I leave this room. The rewrite is private: no class watching, and nobody says the word 'cheating' in front of him. Nothing goes on his record, in writing, from you, by email tonight. And you do this under procedure 4.4, not as a favour. Say yes to those four and I'll stay for the detail. Otherwise I'm walking to the principal's office."
What would make you accept that, and what would make you refuse?

"Yes if the four things are in writing tonight, and if the rewrite is in a room with nobody watching him. No if you stop before the zero comes off, or if you add a condition that puts a mark on him. Say yes or no to the four."
I'll put it in an email tonight to you and the principal. Next Monday at lunch is the earliest I can supervise it. Is that acceptable?

"Monday lunch is too late. Owen's applications are due December 1, and the zero is still on his record until then. Tomorrow after school, or Thursday at the latest, in the room, one period, nobody watching. And the zero comes off the gradebook today, before I leave, not after the rewrite. Say yes to that and to the email, and I'll stay for the detail. If not, I'm going to the principal's office with the times I've written down."
Thursday after school works. I'll take the zero off tonight and send the email with the four points. Yes to all four.

"Okay. Tonight's email to me and the principal, with the four points in writing. The zero off the gradebook tonight, not Thursday. Thursday after school, one period, nobody watching him. Nothing on his record. I'll be reading that email before breakfast, and if any one of those four is missing, I'm in the principal's office Wednesday morning. Put it in writing, Hale."
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Thank you for agreeing today to the four points below. Please confirm in writing tonight that you have done each one.

1. The zero comes off the gradebook tonight, Tuesday, November 10.
2. Owen completes a supervised rewrite of the essay in your room this Thursday, November 12, after school, one period, with no devices and no other students present.
3. If the rewrite shows the learning, its mark replaces the original mark, and nothing is placed in Owen's record, under procedure 4.4.
4. Nothing about this matter goes on Owen's record at any point.

Any missing point means I will raise this with the principal first thing Wednesday morning, and I still ask for a copy of the outline, the September 24 piece and the Folger edition you said you would bring.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position, with the zero withdrawn and a supervised rewrite agreed under procedure 4.4, on her terms.
Moved at: "Okay. Some of that is what I asked for, and some of it isn't yet."
Slipped at: "Two minutes." / "I'm not checking a watch for you." (none; the early concession came at "Ten minutes, Hale." after the November 2 planner page, which gave her nothing to check.)
